POWL is a high-priority underfollowed-lane candidate for medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical solutions; evidence is strong but later layers must test backlog concentration and cyclicality.

MYRG is a plausible underfollowed service-side candidate tied to substations, transmission, and data-center electrical construction; evidence is directional and requires backlog/customer verification.

MYRG should be tracked as an underfollowed second-order grid/EPC candidate for data-center interconnection because its T&D/substation and C&I data-center capabilities map to the power-availability bottleneck, but data-center-specific backlog evidence is still needed.

IESC should be tracked as a mixed-label electrical infrastructure candidate with explicit data-center-driven Infrastructure Solutions growth; later layers should verify customer concentration and backlog quality.

node: Grid interconnection, transformers, switchgear, substations, transmission services, and power availability
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the power-availability node found one high-attention reference anchor and two underfollowed direct-exposure candidates. The clearest direct public-company evidence in this pass is in medium-voltage switchgear, electrical distribution equipment, substation/transmission construction, and data-center electrical services. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation. Layer 1B expansion for the grid/power-availability node found three US-listed candidates with plausible direct or second-order AI data-center exposure. Powell Industries is the cleanest equipment-vendor read-through because its official releases cite medium-voltage switchgear demand, AI/data-center activity, record backlog, and a post-quarter data-center order above $400 million. IES Holdings has direct data-center electrical/technology infrastructure exposure with management stating that data-center demand was a primary growth driver. MYR Group is a specialty electrical contractor with transmission, distribution, substation, and data-center facility services exposure; its AI link is more second-order and needs backlog/customer verification. This is research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Underfollowed expansion for the power-availability node points to three US-listed candidates sitting closer to electrical delivery than to headline AI compute: Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems, MYR Group for transmission/substation and commercial-industrial electrical construction, and IES Holdings for data-center electric
